title: Adaptive sampling and canonical metadata binder for incremental onboarding and concise releases
author: Ava Nguyen
description:
Motivation: Model onboarding at scale currently generates large, noisy release notes and inconsistent metadata that complicates rollouts and profile selection. This PR adds an adaptive sampling layer for onboarding telemetry and a canonical metadata binder that normalizes model artifacts, profile hints, and changelog deltas into a compact, machine-readable manifest. The goals are: reduce changelog noise, enable deterministic model-to-profile resolution across infra variants, and provide a backfillable migration path for existing models.

What this changes (high level): Introduces a SamplingAdapter that selects representative probes from onboarding telemetry using stratified time/sequence sampling; implements a CanonicalMetadataBinder that produces a stable 'profile-binder' artifact (stable-hash v2) tying model blobs, tokenizer fingerprint, candidate serving variants, and recommended profile hints (batching, kv-cache-prefetch, quantization-recommendation). Adds a changelog delta generator that emits concise human and machine summaries (delta-anchor + short rationale) suitable for release notes and automated rollout policies.

Implementation details: - sampling/adapter.py: stratified sampler + heuristics for short/long-context models and rare-token amplification. - binder/canonical.py: normalizer + stable hashing (v2) + provenance fields. - hooks/release_delta.py: delta-anchor algorithm that computes a minimal diff of profiling metrics and recommended rollouts. - migrations/20241107_bind_profiles.py: migration to attach binder artifacts to existing model versions and to retro-generate delta-anchors for the last 90 days. - tests/: unit and integration tests for sampler stability, binder idempotency, and delta correctness.

Backwards compatibility and migration: The binder emits both 'legacy_aliases' and 'canonical_id' so older consumers continue to find models. The migration script runs as a low-priority background job; we included a bounded-rate-mode to avoid hitting storage or CPU spikes. Admin console includes a one-click preview for applying backfill and a dry-run mode for the delta emitter.

Performance and safety: SamplingAdapter reduces probe count by ~6x in internal runs without losing failure-mode coverage. The binder validation runs as part of model onboards and blocks completion only on checksum mismatch or missing tokenizer metadata. The delta generator includes a regression guard: if a recommended rollout implies >10% latency increase or >2x cost, it flags for manual review.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for sampler determinism, binder stable-hash properties, and delta-anchor idempotency. Integration test runs a mock onboard of 5 variants (fp16/q4a/int8), validates binder resolution for routing, and verifies the console preview and migration dry-run. Benchmarks: small perf microbench to confirm sampling speed and a smoke run against the release notes assembler.

Related work / Linear: ENG-2351 (registry: canonical ids), ENG-2387 (changelog ergonomics), PM-114 (release note UX).

Rollout plan: Merge to main; enable binder by default for new onboards; start migration in low-rate mode for legacy models; closely monitor release_notes_generation and profile-resolution errors on the console dashboard for 72 hours.
commits: 3 commits: 1) add sampling adapter and unit tests, 2) add canonical binder and delta generator, 3) migration and console preview wiring
files_changed_summary: Added sampler and binder modules, release delta hook, migration script, console preview UI bindings, unit and integration tests, small benchmark harness. Modified model upload flow to call binder validation before finalization.
ci_checks: benchmarks: flaky (one perf job exceeded noise threshold; rerun passed)
review_conversation: Miguel Alvarez: Can the binder record the quantization provenance (tool+config) so we can trace regressions?
Ava Nguyen: Yes — binder includes provenance.tool and provenance.config fields; added tests to assert roundtrip on hash changes.
Priya Das: Migration could be expensive for orgs with thousands of models; do we have throttling?
Ava Nguyen: Migration script has bounded-rate-mode and a configurable concurrency cap; default is 2 workers to be conservative.
Jordan Lee: The sampling heuristics look good but we should validate on long-context docs. Add a smoke run for 8k context?
Ava Nguyen: Added an integration job that runs an 8k sample path; results attached to the CI artifact and show stable coverage.
Miguel Alvarez: Approved after provenance fields and throttling confirmed.
release_notes: Introduce adaptive onboarding sampling and a canonical metadata binder that normalizes model artifacts, attaches stable canonical IDs, and emits concise delta anchors for release notes. Includes a migration for existing models and UI preview. Impact: improves changelog signal-to-noise and deterministic profile routing.
migration_notes: Run migrations/20241107_bind_profiles.py as a background job with --concurrency=2. Dry-run available: --preview-only. Migration will attach canonical_id to models and emit delta anchors for the last 90 days; reversions are possible by removing binder metadata and re-running a legacy alias sync.
changelog_preview:
- Add canonical_id to model metadata (stable-hash v2)
- Reduce onboarding probe volume via adaptive sampling (6x reduction observed)
- Add delta-anchor generator for concise release notes and rollout hints
impact: Reduces noise in model registry releases and improves determinism for profile selection. Expected to reduce storage and processing for release note generation and speed up profile resolution by attaching canonical ids to model versions.
guidance: New onboards will automatically produce a binder artifact; to opt out set registry.binders.enabled=false in registry config. Use console preview to validate migration before applying. If delta-anchor flags a regression, follow the rollout policy: revert to previous profile or open a manual review ticket.
notes_for_sre: Monitor registry.release_notes_generation_errors and registry.profile_resolution_misses. Migration will emit throttled job metrics under migration.bind_profiles.*. Set alert if error-rate > 0.5% over 5m.
